text: The Deseret Alphabet should be taught and we should pay attention to schooling our children in a way they can understand and learn that they may advance in the history of the world and in all the sciences of the day.
label: General Conference · October 1867
note: Brigham Young, “Texts for the Elders,” General Conference, 7 October 1867, Monday afternoon session.

text: [The Deseret Alphabet] will write Spanish, hebrew, greek, and with the addition of a few more Leters, all the Languages of the Earth.
label: Letter to Orson Pratt · January 1854
note: Parley P. Pratt to Orson Pratt, 30 January 1854, in his own spelling; quoted in Givens & Grow, Parley P. Pratt: The Apostle Paul of Mormonism (2011), 410.

text: [The Deseret Alphabet] will be the means of introducing uniformity in our orthography, and the years that are now required to learn to read and spell can be devoted to other studies.
label: General Conference · October 1868
note: Brigham Young, “Southern Missions—Deseret Alphabet—Relief Societies—Home Manufactures,” General Conference, 8 October 1868; Journal of Discourses 12:298.

text: This, the Deseret Alphabet furnishes, and each one should do all in his power to make it universal.
label: Juvenile Instructor · November 1869
note: George Q. Cannon, editorial, Juvenile Instructor 4 (6 November 1869): 180.

text: [The Deseret Alphabet is] a step and partial return to a pure language which has been promised unto us in the latter days.
label: Letter to Frederick Schonfield · 1858
note: Brigham Young to Frederick Schonfield, 29 November 1858. Brigham Young Center.

text: I think that in all our schools phonetics should form one branch of study.
label: General Conference · October 1867
note: George A. Smith, “Education—Phonetics—Storing Up Grain—Home Manufactures,” General Conference, 9 October 1867; Journal of Discourses 12:140.

text: The Deseret Alphabet should be studied, that our young might advance more rapidly in the knowledge of every science.
label: General Conference · October 1867
note: Brigham Young, General Conference, 7 October 1867, afternoon, as reported in the Deseret News; The Complete Discourses of Brigham Young, 4:2494.

text: An alphabet should contain just as many letters as there are simple-pure atoms of sound.
label: Letter to Brigham Young · August 1854
note: George D. Watt to Brigham Young, 21 August 1854.

text: I hope I may live long enough to see the Deseret Alphabet introduced to supersede the present system of the Autography of our Language.
label: Discourse · July 1866
note: Brigham Young, 15 July 1866, as reported by Wilford Woodruff (his spelling); The Complete Discourses of Brigham Young, 4:2346.

text: In the new alphabet every letter has a fixed and unalterable sound; and every word is spelt with reference to given sounds.
label: “The New Alphabet” · January 1854
note: “The New Alphabet,” Deseret News, 19 January 1854; see Crawley, A Descriptive Bibliography of the Mormon Church, vol. 3.

text: The advantages of this alphabet will soon be realized, especially by foreigners.
label: General Conference · October 1868
note: Brigham Young, “Southern Missions—Deseret Alphabet—Relief Societies—Home Manufactures,” General Conference, 8 October 1868; Journal of Discourses 12:298.

text: The Regency have formed a new Alphabet, which it is expected will prove highly beneficial, in acquiring the English language, to foreigners.
label: Eleventh General Epistle · April 1854
note: Brigham Young, Heber C. Kimball and Jedediah M. Grant, Eleventh General Epistle of the First Presidency, 10 April 1854.

text: I would like to see the orthography introduced which we have adopted in the Deseret Alphabet, which is simple and easy to be understood.
label: Discourse · July 1866
note: Brigham Young, July 1866; The Complete Discourses of Brigham Young, 4:2344.

text: The Regency are getting out a new alphabet; and when we learn our letters ourselves, we will teach others.
label: Discourse · December 1853
note: Parley P. Pratt, “Education,” 26 December 1853; Journal of Discourses 6:253.

text: We wish to introduce this alphabet into our schools. … We have been contemplating this for years.
label: General Conference · October 1868
note: Brigham Young, “Southern Missions—Deseret Alphabet—Relief Societies—Home Manufactures,” General Conference, 8 October 1868; Journal of Discourses 12:298.
